title: Capacity onboarding: SLA banding, GPU class decision matrix, and elastic-fallback choreography
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers requesting reserved GPU capacity frequently arrive with incomplete proxies for required throughput and availability. This leads to oversubscribed pools, missed latency SLAs, or expensive overprovisioning. Goal: create a concise decision artifact and onboarding flow that lets Customer Success + Sales rapidly map a customer's workload characteristics to: (1) SLA banding (99th/95th latency and availability targets), (2) recommended reserved throughput commitment, (3) GPU class recommendation (memory/compute/quantization tradeoffs), and (4) an elastic-fallback choreography (bursting, preemption tolerance, and automated rollout policies). Scope: product guidance, customer-facing questionnaire, CS runbook, implementation acceptance criteria for engineering hooks (routing flags, fallback models, and autoscaling guardrails). Out of scope: implementation of low-level kernel optimizations or new GPU drivers. Success metrics: time-to-provision reduced from 6 days to 2 business days for 80% of enterprise requests; post-onboarding SLA violations reduced by 60% in first 90 days.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A one-page decision matrix mapping workload profiles (qps/avg inference tokens/peak concurrency) to SLA bands and a recommended reserved throughput in tokens/sec or vGPU-equivalent is published and reviewed by CS, Sales, and Eng.
2) A short customer questionnaire (<= 12 fields) that CS can use in the intake call is finalized and added to the intake form template.
3) A runbook for provisioning teams that includes escalation ladder, required telemetry checks, and rollback triggers is published in Confluence.
4) Engineering acceptance criteria defined: routing flag required, fallback model family agreed, and autoscale guardrail thresholds documented so ENG tickets can be scoped.
5) Pilot with two customers (one RLHF-heavy, one high-concurrency embedding workload) completed and feedback captured in comments before wide rollout.

decisions: Use a three-tier SLA banding (Bronze/Silver/Gold) mapped to concrete availability and 95th/99th latency targets to simplify negotiations with Sales.
Represent recommended throughput as both tokens/sec and a vGPU-equivalent number to bridge Sales/Infra conversations.

Default GPU-class recommendation will prefer lower-cost quantized paths for embedding-heavy workloads and higher-memory H100-class for long-sequence RLHF workloads; final mapping documented in matrix.

Implement an elastic-fallback choreography that: primary route -> reserved pool; secondary route -> compatible quantized model family in shared pool; tertiary route -> queued/batch processing with customer consent.
